extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and legal scholars interested in Brazilian patent prosecution and INPI procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, requirements, and procedural standards governing filing, examination, publication, appeals, nullity, and post-grant matters before Brazil's INPI under the LPI (Law No. 9,279/96) and related INPI normative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a patent application (Article 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application must contain: I – request; II – specifications; III – claims; IV – drawings, if applicable; V – abstract; and VI – proof of payment of the filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms required to file are available from INPI’s website. Minimum conditions for accepting a filing include technical content, the application, and proof of payment of the filing fee (Article 21). If insufficient but containing data on object, applicant and inventor, the INPI may issue requirements to be met within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient description / enablement (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the patent must be sufficiently described in the specifications, clearly and completely, to allow its reproduction by a person skilled in the art and must indicate, when appropriate, the best way to execute it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When biological material is essential and not publicly available, the report must be supplemented with deposit of material at an INPI-authorized or internationally recognized depositary (Budapest Treaty), and such data must integrate the specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements and initial acceptance (Articles 19–21)
rubrics_metrics.description: INPI verifies minimum conditions for accepting a patent application (technical content, application, proof of payment); formal requirements not met are published and must be met within 30 days or the filing may be returned or dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order Codes indicate progress (e.g., Order Code 2.5 for formal requirements). If formal requirements are met, Order Code 2.1 is notified and filing date is the date of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney and representation requirements (Article 216)
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of attorney must be in Portuguese (original, transcript or authenticated photocopy); consular authentication and notarization are not required. It must be submitted within 60 days from the date of the first act of the party in the proceedings, under penalty of dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal of the patent application for failure to submit the power of attorney is final. Some petitions and filings have specific form requirements available on INPI’s website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign applicants must appoint attorney-in-fact in Brazil (Article 217)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applicants are required to appoint and maintain an attorney-in-fact in Brazil with powers to represent them in administrative and judicial proceedings, including to receive service of process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to maintain such representation may affect proceedings; power of attorney rules (Portuguese language, 60‑day submission) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art / novelty definition (Article 11(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: State of the art refers to everything accessible to the public before the filing date by written or oral description, by use or any other means, in Brazil or abroad, excluding what is kept under industrial secret (with exceptions in Articles 12, 16, 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty requires the object be beyond the state of the art. INPI recommends a preliminary search before filing to assess novelty and inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished Brazilian applications as prior art for novelty (Article 11(2)–(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The full content of an application filed in Brazil and not yet published is considered state of the art from the date of filing or priority claimed, provided it is published, but only for the analysis of the novelty requirement, not for inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision also applies to international applications with national processing in Brazil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for inventor-originated disclosures (Article 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third party discloses the invention in the 12 months preceding the filing or priority date based on information obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or as a result of acts performed by the inventor (or by INPI publication without consent), a grace period will be considered and will not affect novelty assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INPI may require a statement from the inventor concerning the disclosure, possibly accompanied by evidence, under regulatory conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim and evidence deadlines (Article 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: A priority claim is made upon filing and may be supplemented within 60 days by other priorities prior to the Brazilian filing date; it must be supported by a document of origin and translation as required. If proof is not presented at filing, it must be provided within 180 days; translations for internationals must be provided within 60 days of national processing starting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Brazilian filing is faithfully contained in the document of origin, a statement by the applicant may replace the translation. Failure to provide evidence within the time limits results in loss of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential processing for national defense subject matter (Article 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications whose subject matter is of interest to national defense are processed confidentially and not subject to ordinary LPI provisions; filing or disclosure abroad is prohibited unless authorized, and exploitation/assignment depend on prior authorization; indemnity is guaranteed when rights are restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applications are excluded from ordinary publication and processing; violation (e.g., filing abroad without authorization) is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and content (Articles 30, 226)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are kept secret for 18 months from the filing date or earliest priority date and are published thereafter in the RPI, unless early publication is requested. Publication must contain data identifying the application and make available specifications, claims, abstract and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request early publication; biological material referenced under Article 24(1) becomes available to the public upon publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments before examination (Article 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may amend the application up until the request for examination, provided that amendments are limited to the subject matter initially disclosed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments beyond the originally disclosed subject matter are not permitted; this limits added matter before examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination timing (Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: The substantive examination of the patent application must be requested by the applicant or any interested party within 36 months of the filing date, under penalty of dismissal of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon notification of dismissal for failure to request examination, the applicant has 60 days to pay a reinstatement fee together with a request for examination to restore the application (Order Code 11.1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials to be submitted upon examination request or when requested (Article 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once examination is requested, the following must be submitted within 60 days when requested: I – objections, search for prior art and examination results for corresponding applications when priority is claimed; II – documents required for regularization and examination; III – a simple translation of the appropriate priority document if replaced by a declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required documents within the 60‑day period may lead to dismissal of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and results of technical/substantive examination (Article 35–36)
rubrics_metrics.description: During technical examination, a search report and opinion are prepared concerning: I – patentability; II – suitability of the application given the nature claimed; III – reformulation of the application or division; IV – technical requirements. If the opinion finds non-patentability or issues requirements, the applicant is notified to provide comments within 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches are conducted by engineers and technicians across technological fields and may include worldwide prior art. Any interested party may submit comments and documents during this stage. If requirements are not met, the application will be definitively dismissed; if answered, the examination proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible examination outcomes and Order Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination may conclude the application is patentable (Order Code 9.1); that it must be adapted, reformulated/divided, or meet technical requirements (Order Code 6.1); or that the application is unpatentable (Order Code 7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fulfillment of requirements must be met within time determined by Article 36 (within 90 days). Once examination is concluded, a decision is rendered granting or rejecting the application (Article 37).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative nullity grounds (Article 50) and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent’s nullity is declared administratively when: I – any one of the legal requirements has not been met; II – the specifications and the claims do not comply with Articles 24 and 25 respectively; III – the subject matter extends beyond the content of the application originally filed; IV – any formalities essential to the granting have not been met during processing. Nullity may be partial if remaining claims are patentable; nullity takes effect from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullity proceedings may be filed by the INPI on its own initiative or by any person with legitimate interest within six months from grant (Article 51). Proceedings continue even if the patent has terminated (ex tunc effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullity administrative procedure / due process (Articles 51–57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once nullity proceedings are filed, due process is followed: patent holders may make a statement within 60 days; INPI issues an opinion and notifies holder and claimant within the same period; the INPI’s president decides and decision is published once final and unappealable to notify third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullity proceedings continue regardless of patent term expiry; partial nullity possible if remaining claims are independently patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals in administrative phase and time limits (Articles 212–220, 213–215)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals against INPI decisions must be filed within 60 days and are entertained with supersedeas and full review effects. A decision that determines definitive dismissal of a patent application or that grants a patent application or certificate of addition is unappealable (Article 212(2)). Appeals are decided by the INPI’s president and may be final and unappealable (Article 215).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition will not be entertained if submitted after the time limit or not accompanied by proof of payment of the respective fee (Article 218). A petition, opposition, or appeal will not be entertained if late, lacks legal grounds, or lacks the fee (Article 219). INPI may impose requirements to complement appeal briefs, to be met within 60 days (Article 214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines counting rules (Articles 221–224)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits for administrative proceedings are continuous, automatically extinguishing right to act after expiry unless a just cause is shown. In counting time limits, the start day is excluded and the due date included; time limits start being counted from the first business day after notification (publication in INPI's official body). If no express determination exists, 60 days is the default time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Just cause requires demonstration that an unexpected event beyond a party's will prevented performance. Judicial proceedings are governed by the CPC with specific counting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's duty to monitor prosecution and notification channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must regularly consult the RPI (Revista da Propriedade Industrial) to monitor their applications using the assigned number. PUSH-INPI can register processes and receive publications by email but does not replace RPI follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for a patent application is notified in RPI with Order Code 2.10; publication and other Order Codes indicate processing stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and abandonment publication and timing (Article 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: A withdrawn or abandoned patent application must be published. A request for withdrawal must be submitted within 16 months of the filing date or earliest priority date. Withdrawal of a previous filing without producing effect gives priority to the immediately subsequent filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of withdrawal makes the subject matter available in the public domain if reinstatement is not requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees for issuance of letters patent (Order Codes 9.1, 11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant or patent holder has 60 days (ordinary term) from publication of the granting in the RPI to present evidence of payment of the fee for issuance of letters patent. Payment may be made within 30 days (extraordinary term) from the end of the previous term by payment of a specific fee, under penalty of final dismissal of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR Resolution No. 13 regulates delivery of letters patent in electronic format and other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term restoration and reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent holder may request the restoration of an application or patent within three months from the date of publication of the shelving in the RPI or from the expiry of the patent; the holder must prove that the annual fee and restoration fee have been paid. Failure to request restoration leads to definitive shelving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement after dismissal for failure to request examination must be sought within 60 days with payment of reinstatement fee (Order Code 11.1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use/exploitation requirement and compulsory licensing (Articles 68, 80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three years of the grant of the patent, the patent holder must start exploiting or commercializing the product and exercising their right; otherwise the holder may be subject to having the patent compulsorily licensed. A compulsorily licensed patent may lapse for lack of exploitation if, after two years from the first compulsory license, the nonuse is not justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licensing is a statutory mechanism to address nonuse; justification or evidence of exploitation can forestall compulsory licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on amendment and added matter (Article 32 / Article 50(III))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are allowed up to the request for examination but must be limited to the subject matter initially disclosed; a ground for administrative nullity is that the subject matter of the patent extends beyond the content of the application originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added matter is a basis for nullity and is assessed with ex tunc effects if nullity declared.
